Contact our Albuquerque, NM, law office to learn more about working with our award-winning law firm. Your initial case evaluation is free. How Does New Mexico Define Wrongful Death? When you’re injured in an accident in New Mexico, you’ll typically have the right to seek compensation from an at-fault or liable party. The right to seek damages does not disappear when a victim dies from their injuries. Instead, the ability to seek compensation shifts to another party through what’s called a wrongful death claim. Under New Mexico law, a wrongful death occurs when a person is killed because of the “wrongful act, neglect or default of another” and the victim would have had the right to sue if they’d survived. In these situations, the personal representative of the victim’s estate can file a wrongful death claim to recover compensation on behalf of the victim’s surviving family members. Damages are awarded to the estate and distributed to the spouse, children, grandchildren, and/or parents. What Types of Damages Can Be Awarded in an ALBUQUERQUE Wrongful Death Case? When you file a wrongful death lawsuit in New Mexico, you’ll have the right to seek compensatory and exemplary damages. Compensatory damages help to cover financial losses associated with the victim’s death (economic awards), as well as harder-to-value struggles (non-economic damages), such as: Costs associated with the victim’s funeral and burial Medical expenses incurred prior to the victim’s death Lost wages and benefits the victim would have earned if they’d survived The value of the victim’s household services and support Property damage related to the victim’s fatal accident A parent, child, or spouse’s emotional distress Loss of consortium The victim’s pain and suffering prior to death Exemplary damages, also known as punitive damages, are awarded to punish a defendant for conduct that is grossly negligent or wilful. Most often, these are reserved for particularly heinous acts, like drunk driving or intentional concealment of a product’s known dangers. Will the Decedent’s Shared Fault Impact a Wrongful Death Settlement in ALBUQUERQUE? Yes. New Mexico’s pure comparative negligence law applies to civil personal injury cases, including matters of wrongful death. If your family member was partly responsible for their fatal accident or injury, their shared fault will impact your family’s wrongful death case. A settlement or jury award will be reduced based on their proportionate share of the blame. Singleton Schreiber will be ready to defend your family member’s name and fight back against any claims of contributory negligence that could hurt your case.
